feature: FNIT TorchFLIRT weighted 12-DOF correlation-ratio runtime diagnosis
claim_boundary: Single real-data, shared-node diagnostic; timings are observations, not a hardware-wide speed claim.

cprofile.note: Cumulative times overlap and must not be summed.

gpu_sampling.interpretation: The workload is limited by serial candidate generation, small-kernel launch overhead, and host-device synchronization rather than peak GPU arithmetic throughput.

cpu_diagnostic.interpretation: Pure PyTorch CPU is not a competitive default for this implementation.

implementation_findings: The Brent coordinate search chooses the next point from the preceding cost, preventing one global batch of all evaluations.
Weighted cost evaluates both the moving FA and moving weight with manual trilinear interpolation.
CUDA scalar conversion to Python bool or float introduces repeated host-device synchronization.
FSL-order interpolation and arithmetic are expressed as many pointwise and indexed PyTorch operations rather than one fused kernel.
TF32 does not accelerate the dominant interpolation, indexing, segmented reduction, and Python-controlled search operations.
optimization_order: Batch independent fine angular candidates in bounded chunks.
Fuse coordinate generation, two trilinear gathers, boundary weighting, and correlation-ratio accumulation in a compiled CUDA or Triton kernel.
Keep scalar stopping decisions on device where possible and synchronize once per optimizer decision.
Revalidate matrix and moved-image outputs against the ten-case unweighted suite and the weighted FA case after each change.
